scenes.title: The barre
scenes.subtitle: Your first full F.
lines: This lesson teaches your first full F barre chord — the foundation for many songs to come.

scenes.heading: How to barre
points: Pull back gently with your arm
Weeks of practice to sound clean
lines: A barre is when your index finger presses several strings at once, flat across the fretboard.
Roll your finger slightly onto its bony side, keep it just behind the fret, and pull back gently with your arm.
It takes time — weeks — to sound clean.
Keep practicing, and you'll get there.
The F major barre chord is a great first step — let's place your fingers one by one.
Lay finger 1 flat across fret 1, from string 6 to string 1.
Here's how it sounds: strummed, then string by string.
scenes.tip: Lay finger 1 flat across all six strings at fret 1, rolled slightly onto its bony side. Pull back with your arm instead of squeezing with your thumb.

scenes.heading: Fixing buzzes
points: Slide finger toward headstock or body
lines: Check your F barre one string at a time.
If a string buzzes, it may sit in a crease of your index finger.
Slide the finger slightly toward the headstock or body, or roll it gently until the note rings clear.
Small adjustments make a big difference — you've got this!
Let's practice changing between C major and F major.
Move your fingers smoothly and keep the rhythm steady.

points: Pull back gently with your arm
lines: Press flat, roll gently, and keep practicing — the app is here to listen and help you sound your best.
